Common_Names_Hindi: High BP; Raktchap; BP ki bimari
Primary_Symptoms: Often asymptomatic; Mild headache; Dizziness; Epistaxis
Secondary_Symptoms: Palpitations; Fatigue; Visual blurring; Tinnitus
Clarifying_Questions: 1. BP kitna rehta hai (130-139 / 80-89 mm Hg)?; 2. Sirdard ya chakkar aate hain?; 3. Diabetes ya Kidney ki bimari hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Telmisartan OR Amlodipine
Supportive_Medicines: Low-sodium diet; Regular exercise
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Contraindicated in pregnancy; Avoid NSAIDs (worsen BP, use Paracetamol); Telmisartan requires potassium/renal function monitoring; Amlodipine may cause ankle swelling
Home_Care_Advice: Reduce daily salt intake (<5g/day); Exercise 30 mins daily; Avoid smoking, alcohol, and stress; Maintain ideal weight
Lab_Investigations: BP monitoring chart; Serum Creatinine & Electrolytes; Urine Routine/Microalbumin; ECG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; BP >180/120 mm Hg; Severe chest pain; Breathlessness; Severe thunderclap headache; Neurological deficits

Common_Names_Hindi: Tez High BP; High BP Stage 2
Primary_Symptoms: Occipital morning headache; Dizziness; Fatigue; Chest tightness
Secondary_Symptoms: Palpitations; Shortness of breath on exertion; Epistaxis; Visual changes
Clarifying_Questions: 1. BP kitna hai (≥140 / ≥90 mm Hg)?; 2. Subah uthte hi sirdard hota hai?; 3. BP ki koi dawai pehle se chal rahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Telmisartan + Amlodipine OR Telmisartan + Hydrochlorothiazide
Supportive_Medicines: Potassium/Renal monitoring; Low-salt diet
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Contraindicated in pregnancy, hyperkalemia, and bilateral renal artery stenosis; Avoid NSAIDs; Diuretics require hydration/electrolyte monitoring; Amlodipine may cause ankle swelling
Home_Care_Advice: Strict low-sodium diet (<3-5g/day); Daily home BP tracking; Regular aerobic exercise; Zero tobacco/alcohol
Lab_Investigations: Serum Electrolytes (Sodium, Potassium); Serum Creatinine; HbA1c; Lipid Profile; ECG; Echocardiogram
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; BP >180/120 mm Hg; Chest pain radiating to arm/jaw; Acute dyspnea; Confusion; Sudden vision loss

Common_Names_Hindi: Kewal Upar ka BP Bada Hona
Primary_Symptoms: High Systolic BP (≥140 mm Hg) with Normal Diastolic (<90 mm Hg) in elderly; Head heaviness
Secondary_Symptoms: Dizziness; Unsteadiness; Fatigue; Pulsatile tinnitus
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kewal upar waala BP bada rehta hai?; 2. Umar 60 saal se zyada hai?; 3. Chakkar ya bhari-pan mehsoos hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Amlodipine OR Chlorthalidone / Telmisartan
Supportive_Medicines: Low-salt diet; Moderate walking
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Amlodipine may cause ankle swelling; Chlorthalidone requires electrolyte monitoring (hypokalemia/hyponatremia risk); Avoid NSAIDs; Caution in gout with diuretics
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid sudden standing to prevent orthostatic dizziness; Low-salt diet; Regular gentle walking; Daily BP recording
Lab_Investigations: Serum Electrolytes; Serum Uric Acid; Serum Creatinine; ECG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Systolic BP >180 mm Hg; Syncope; Chest pain; Dizziness causing falls; Transient ischemic attack signs

Common_Names_Hindi: Kabu me na aane waala High BP
Primary_Symptoms: BP remains >140/90 mm Hg despite 3 full-dose antihypertensives (including a diuretic); Headaches
Secondary_Symptoms: Dizziness; Nocturia; Fatigue; Pedal edema
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Teen dawaiyo ke baad bhi BP bada rehta hai?; 2. Ek dawai paani ki (diuretic) hai?; 3. Kidney ya snoring ki bimari hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Spironolactone (added to Triple Therapy under Specialist)
Supportive_Medicines: Specialist-led triple/quadruple therapy adjustments
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; High risk of hyperkalemia and gynecomastia with Spironolactone; Contraindicated in severe CKD (eGFR <30) and Addison's disease; Avoid NSAIDs
Home_Care_Advice: Strict salt restriction (<3g/day); Screen for secondary causes (Sleep Apnea, Renal Artery Stenosis); Take meds strictly on time
Lab_Investigations: Serum Potassium & Creatinine (frequent); Renal Artery Doppler USG; Plasma Aldosterone/Renin Ratio; Polysomnography
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; BP >180/120 mm Hg; Hyperkalemia symptoms (muscle weakness, bradycardia); Acute pulmonary edema; Chest pain

Primary_Symptoms: Elevated BP strictly in clinical/hospital setting; Normal BP at home (<135/85 mm Hg)
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild anxiety in clinic; Normal home readings; Absence of end-organ damage
Clarifying_Questions: 1. BP kewal doctor ke clinic me bada aata hai?; 2. Ghar par BP normal rehta hai?; 3. Ghabraahat hoti hai hospital me?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Reassurance & Lifestyle Modification (No Primary Drug unless true HTN develops)
Supportive_Medicines: Home BP Logbook; Relaxation techniques
Precautions_Contraindications: Do not start lifelong antihypertensives based solely on single clinic readings; Avoid excessive anxiety; Monitor home readings regularly
Home_Care_Advice: Keep a 7-day home BP diary (morning/evening); Practice deep breathing before clinic visits; Limit caffeine before BP measurement
Lab_Investigations: 24-hour Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring (ABPM - Gold Standard); Home Blood Pressure Monitoring (HBPM) log
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Home BP readings persistently >135/85 mm Hg; Onset of symptoms like severe headache, chest pain, or vision changes

Primary_Symptoms: Severe BP elevation (>180/120 mm Hg) with acute target organ damage (headache, dyspnea, chest pain)
Secondary_Symptoms: Confusion; Seizures; Epistaxis; Vomiting; Papilledema; Oliguria
Clarifying_Questions: 1. BP 180/120 se upar hai?; 2. Severe sirdard, saans phoolna ya chhati me dard hai?; 3. Behoshi ya ulti hui hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Labetalol; Injection Nitroglycerin; Injection Sodium Nitroprusside
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency IV titration in ICU
Supportive_Medicines: ICU admission; Parenteral antihypertensives; Continuous intra-arterial BP monitoring
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT lower BP rapidly with oral short-acting nifedipine (causes stroke/MI); Avoid home self-medication
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to hospital ICU; Keep patient calm and resting in semi-reclining position; Do NOT give oral meds at home
Lab_Investigations: Serum Creatinine; Troponin-I; Chest X-ray; CT Brain; Fundoscopy (papilledema); ECG; ABG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; BP >180/120 with confusion, chest pain, breathlessness, or neurological deficits

Primary_Symptoms: Co-existing high BP and high blood sugar; Often asymptomatic; Fatigue; Nocturia
Secondary_Symptoms: Pedal edema; Microalbuminuria; Dizziness; Diminished vision
Clarifying_Questions: 1. BP aur Diabetes dono ki bimari hai?; 2. Peshab me protein (albumin) aata hai?; 3. Pairo me sujan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Telmisartan OR Ramipril (ACEi / ARB primary choice for renal protection)
Supportive_Medicines: Metformin; SGLT2 inhibitors (Empagliflozin); Low-salt diet
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; ACEi/ARBs contraindicated in pregnancy, hyperkalemia, and bilateral renal artery stenosis; Requires K+ and creatinine checks; Avoid NSAIDs
Home_Care_Advice: Target BP <130/80 mm Hg; Strict glycemic control; Low-salt, low-sugar diet; Regular foot care and kidney screening
Lab_Investigations: Serum Creatinine & Potassium; Urinary Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (UACR); HbA1c; Lipid Profile; Fundoscopy
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; BP >180/120 mm Hg; Hypoglycemia; Sudden drop in urine output; Chest pain; Foot ulcers

Primary_Symptoms: Co-existing high BP and chronic kidney disease; Pedal edema; Puffiness of face; Fatigue
Secondary_Symptoms: Anemia; Oliguria; Nocturia; Nausea; Loss of appetite
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kidney ki bimari (CKD) ke sath High BP hai?; 2. Pairo aur chehre par sujan rehti hai?; 3. Creatinine kitna hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Telmisartan OR Amlodipine (under Nephrologist guidance)
Supportive_Medicines: Loop diuretics (Furosemide); Erythropoietin; Phosphate binders
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; ACEi/ARBs require close renal/potassium monitoring (stop if K+ >5.5 or creatinine rises >30%); Avoid NSAIDs strictly (use Paracetamol)
Home_Care_Advice: Strict low-sodium (<2g/day) and low-potassium diet as advised; Fluid restriction if edematous; Avoid OTC painkillers completely
Lab_Investigations: Serum Creatinine & eGFR; Serum Potassium; 24-hour Urinary Protein; Complete Blood Count; Renal USG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Hyperkalemia symptoms (arrhythmia, severe weakness); Acute fluid overload (breathlessness); Oliguria/Anuria; Confusion

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden drop in BP on standing; Postural dizziness; Lightheadedness; Blurred vision
Secondary_Symptoms: Unsteadiness; Presyncope; Syncope; Fatigue; Neck/shoulder pain ('coat-hanger' pain)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khade hote hi chakkar aate hain ya aankho ke aage andhera aata hai?; 2. BP ki dawai khaate hain?; 3. Paspados me behoshi hui hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Midodrine OR Fludrocortisone (under Specialist guidance)
Dosage_Frequency: TDS (Midodrine, last dose 4h before bed) / OD (Fludrocortisone)
Supportive_Medicines: Abdominal binders; Compression stockings; Increased salt/water intake
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Midodrine causes severe supine hypertension (do not take last dose near bedtime or lie flat); Fludrocortisone causes fluid retention and hypokalemia
Home_Care_Advice: Change positions slowly (sit before standing); Elevate head of bed by 10-15 degrees; Drink 500 mL water before standing; Use waist-high compression stockings
Lab_Investigations: Postural BP monitoring (lying vs 3-min standing); ECG; Serum Electrolytes; HbA1c (rule out diabetic neuropathy)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Syncope causing head injury/trauma; Chest pain; Persistent vertigo; Neurological deficits

Primary_Symptoms: Low BP (<90/60 mm Hg) with symptoms: fatigue, dizziness, weakness, fainting
Secondary_Symptoms: Cold clammy skin; Blurred vision; Confusion; Tachycardia; Nausea
Clarifying_Questions: 1. BP 90/60 se kam rehta hai?; 2. Bahut kamzori, chakkar ya thakan lagti hai?; 3. Dast, ulti ya paani ki kami hui hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) + Hydration (No routine primary drug unless shock)
Supportive_Medicines: Midodrine 2.5 mg TDS (only if chronic severe symptomatic orthostatic hypotension under doctor)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rule out underlying shock, sepsis, internal bleeding, or endocrine crisis before treating as simple low BP; Do not self-medicate with pressor agents
Home_Care_Advice: Increase fluid intake (2.5-3 L/day); Take ORS/lemon salt water; Avoid prolonged standing or sudden standing; Eat small frequent meals
Lab_Investigations: Complete Blood Count; Serum Electrolytes; Cortisol level; Thyroid Function Test; ECG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; BP <80/50 mm Hg; Signs of shock (cold clammy extremities, confusion, oliguria); Hematemesis or black stools

Primary_Symptoms: Exertional retrosternal chest pressure/heaviness relieved by rest or Sublingual Nitroglycerin
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain radiating to left arm, neck, jaw, or epigastrium; Dyspnea on exertion; Diaphoresis
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chalne/mehnat karne par chhati me bhari-pan aata hai?; 2. Aaram karne par 5-10 min me teek hota hai?; 3. Nitroglycerin tab se aaram milta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Isosorbide Mononitrate OR Metoprolol + Sublingual Nitroglycerin SOS
Dosage_Frequency: BD (Isosorbide with 7h asymmetrical gap) / OD (Metoprolol) / SOS sublingual
Supportive_Medicines: Aspirin 75 mg OD; Atorvastatin 40 mg OD; Sublingual Sorbitrate SOS
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Nitrates STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED with Sildenafil/Tadalafil (PDE5 inhibitors) due to fatal shock; Beta blockers caution in asthma/severe bradycardia
Home_Care_Advice: Stop physical exertion immediately during attack; Put 1 Sorbitrate tablet under tongue SOS; Maintain nitrate-free interval (7-8h gap) to prevent tolerance; Low-fat diet
Lab_Investigations: Treadmill Exercise Stress Test (TMT); Stress Echocardiogram; Coronary Angiography; Lipid Profile; ECG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Angina occurring at rest or with decreasing threshold (Unstable Angina); Pain lasting >20 mins not relieved by 3 Sorbitrate tabs (Heart Attack)

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden severe crushing retrosternal chest pain (>20 min) radiating to left arm/jaw; Diaphoresis; Dyspnea
Secondary_Symptoms: Nausea; Vomiting; Impending doom; Syncope; Hypotension or Hypertension; Arrhythmias
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chhati me severe ghutan/dard 20 min se zyada se hai?; 2. Pasiina bohut aa raha hai?; 3. Dard baaye haath ya jabde me jata hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral (Chew Aspirin 300 mg SOS if no allergy/bleeding)
Dosage_Frequency: Single immediate chewable dose at onset while calling emergency services
Supportive_Medicines: Primary PCI (Angioplasty) or Thrombolysis (Streptokinase/Tenecteplase); Dual Antiplatelets; Oxygen; Morphine
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; CHEW ONE 300-325 MG ASPIRIN ONLY IF NOT ALLERGIC AND NO KNOWN BLEEDING DISORDER, WHILE CALLING EMERGENCY SERVICES; Avoid delay
Home_Care_Advice: Call emergency cardiac ambulance immediately; Chew 300 mg Aspirin tab; Keep patient resting motionless; Do NOT drive self to hospital
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG (ST elevation/depression); Cardiac Biomarkers (Troponin-I / Troponin-T); Echocardiogram; Coronary Angiography
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Any suspected heart attack; Cardiac arrest; Severe pulmonary edema; Cardiogenic shock

Common_Names_Hindi: Heart ki nali ki bimari; CAD
Primary_Symptoms: History of angina, stent, or CABG; Exertional dyspnea; Chest discomfort on heavy exertion
Secondary_Symptoms: Fatigue; Palpitations; Anxiety; Reduced exercise tolerance
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Heart me stent/bypass hua hai ya nali me blockage hai?; 2. Daily routine me chalne par takleef hoti hai?; 3. BP/Cholesterol bada hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aspirin + Atorvastatin + Metoprolol / Telmisartan
Supportive_Medicines: Sublingual Nitroglycerin 5 mg SOS; Clopidogrel 75 mg (if dual antiplatelet indicated); Anti-anginals
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Aspirin GI bleeding caution; Statins contraindicated in active liver disease (check LFT, report muscle pain); Beta blockers caution in asthma
Home_Care_Advice: Strict heart-healthy Mediterranean/low-fat diet; Regular 30-min walking (cardiac rehab); Complete smoking cessation; Weight and stress control
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG; Echocardiography; Lipid Profile; Fasting Blood Sugar; Serum Creatinine & LFT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Rest chest pain or sudden increase in angina frequency/severity; Syncope; Acute breathlessness; Bleeding signs

Common_Names_Hindi: Heart Attack ke baad ki dekhbhal
Primary_Symptoms: Post-Myocardial Infarction recovery phase; Absence of acute rest pain; Mild exertional dyspnea
Secondary_Symptoms: Fatigue; Anxiety; Reduced stamina; Mild pedal edema
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Heart attack aae hue kitna samay hua hai?; 2. Stent ya Bypass hua tha?; 3. Sabhi dawaiya niyamit kha rahe hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aspirin + Clopidogrel + Atorvastatin + Metoprolol + Ramipril
Supportive_Medicines: Sublingual Sorbitrate SOS; Cardiac Rehabilitation program; SGLT2 inhibitors
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 150 mg Aspirin / 80 mg Atorvastatin / 10 mg Ramipril
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; High bleeding risk with Dual Antiplatelets (report black stools/bruising); ACEi/ARBs require K+/creatinine checks; Statins require LFT checks
Home_Care_Advice: Cardiac rehabilitation exercise under guidance; Strict adherence to antiplatelet drugs without missing doses; Low-salt, low-fat diet; Complete smoking cessation
Lab_Investigations: Echocardiography (LVEF assessment); ECG; Lipid Profile; HbA1c; Serum Creatinine & Electrolytes
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Recurrent chest pain; Black tarry stools or heavy bleeding; Severe breathlessness; Syncope; Ankle swelling surge

Common_Names_Hindi: Heart ki kamzori; Dil ki sujan
Primary_Symptoms: Exertional dyspnea; Orthopnea (breathlessness on lying flat); Fatigue; Bilateral pedal edema
Secondary_Symptoms: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Dyspnea (PND); Persistent cough/wheeze; Right upper quadrant pain; Weight gain
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Thoda chalne ya letne par saans phoolti hai?; 2. Raat ko achanak saans phoolne se neend khulti hai?; 3. Pairo me sujan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Sacubitril/Valsartan OR Ramipril + Metoprolol Succinate + Furosemide + Dapagliflozin
Supportive_Medicines: Spironolactone 25 mg OD; Digoxin (if AF co-exists); Salt restriction
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Sacubitril/Valsartan contraindicated with ACE inhibitors (must allow 36h wash-out); Furosemide requires electrolyte/dehydration monitoring; Avoid NSAIDs
Home_Care_Advice: Monitor daily body weight (report >1.5 kg gain in 2 days); Strict fluid restriction (1.5 L/day); Salt intake <2g/day; Avoid NSAIDs strictly
Lab_Investigations: Echocardiogram (LVEF %); NT-proBNP / BNP; Serum Electrolytes (Sodium, Potassium); Serum Creatinine; Chest X-ray
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Acute severe dyspnea at rest; Sudden weight gain with worsening leg swelling; Pink frothy sputum; Syncope; Confusion

Common_Names_Hindi: Heart Failure Emergency; Acute Pulmonary Edema
Primary_Symptoms: Severe acute dyspnea at rest; Orthopnea; Pink frothy sputum; Severe bilateral rales/wheezing; Cyanosis
Secondary_Symptoms: Diaphoresis; Tachycardia; Cold clammy extremities; Anxiety; Jugular venous distension; Hypotension/Hypertension
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Achanak letne par saans bilkul ruk rahi hai?; 2. Khansi me gulabi jhaag-waala balgam aata hai?; 3. Pairo aur pet me severe sujan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Furosemide; Injection Nitroglycerin; Injection Dobutamine / Noradrenaline
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency IV administration in ICU
Supportive_Medicines: High-flow Oxygen / Non-Invasive Ventilation (CPAP/BiPAP); IV Loop Diuretics (Furosemide); IV Vasodilators/Inotropes
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT give oral fluids or home medications; Strict upright sitting position while transporting
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency cardiac ambulance transfer; Sit patient strictly upright with legs dangling off bed/trolley; Do NOT give oral water
Lab_Investigations: Chest X-ray (pulmonary congestion/bat-wing edema); NT-proBNP; Arterial Blood Gas (ABG); Echocardiogram; Serum Electrolytes & Creatinine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Acute pulmonary edema; Severe hypoxemic respiratory failure; Cardiogenic shock

Common_Names_Hindi: Dil ki dhadkan be-taal hona; AFib
Primary_Symptoms: Irregularly irregular heart palpitations; Exertional dyspnea; Fatigue; Dizziness
Secondary_Symptoms: Chest discomfort; Presyncope; Anxiety; Reduced exercise tolerance
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dil ki dhadkan bilkul be-taal (irregular) chalti hai?; 2. Chati me dhak-dhak aur chakkar aate hain?; 3. Blood thinner ki dawai chal rahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Metoprolol / Diltiazem (for Rate Control) + Apixaban / Dabigatran (for Anticoagulation)
Supportive_Medicines: Digoxin 0.25 mg OD (under specialist); Amiodarone (if rhythm control needed)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 100 mg Metoprolol / 180 mg Diltiazem / 10 mg Apixaban
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; High bleeding risk with Anticoagulants (report hematuria, black stools, head injury); Beta blockers caution in severe asthma; Diltiazem contraindicated in HFrEF
Home_Care_Advice: Take rate control and anticoagulant meds strictly on time; Avoid binge alcohol ('holiday heart syndrome'); Monitor pulse regularly; Avoid contact sports on blood thinners
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG (absent P waves, irregular RR intervals); Holter Monitoring; Echocardiogram; PT/INR (if Warfarin used); CBC; Renal Function Test
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Sudden stroke signs (facial droop, arm weakness, slurred speech); Heavy bleeding; Ventricular rate >150 bpm at rest; Syncope; Severe chest pain

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden onset and offset of rapid, regular palpitations (150-220 bpm); Lightheadedness; Neck pounding
Secondary_Symptoms: Chest tightness; Dyspnea; Anxiety; Polyuria post episode; Presyncope
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dhadkan achanak bahut tez (150-200) hoti hai aur achanak teek hoti hai?; 2. Gale me dhak-dhak lagti hai?; 3. Chakkar aate hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Adenosine (Emergency Acute termination) OR Verapamil / Metoprolol (Maintenance)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV bolus in ER / BD or TDS (Verapamil)
Supportive_Medicines: Vagal maneuvers (Valsalva, cold ice water face dip); Radiofrequency Catheter Ablation (curative specialist procedure)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Adenosine produces transient 1-3 sec asystole/chest tightness (warn patient); Verapamil strictly CONTRAINDICATED in WPW syndrome with AF and in HFrEF
Home_Care_Advice: Perform vagal maneuvers (bearing down like bowel movement, ice water on face) at onset; Avoid caffeine, nicotine, and alcohol triggers; Seek ER if pulse >150 persists
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG during attack (narrow complex tachycardia without P waves); Baseline ECG; Holter Monitor; Echocardiogram; Electrophysiology Study (EPS)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Palpitations with syncope/fainting; Severe chest pain; Breathlessness; BP drop during attack; SVT episode >30 mins non-responsive to vagal maneuvers

Primary_Symptoms: Regular fast heart rate (>100 bpm) with normal P wave morphology; Palpitations; Anxiety
Secondary_Symptoms: Exercise intolerance; Mild breathlessness; Lightheadedness; Sweating
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Heart beat 100 se upar hai par Taal (rhythm) normal hai?; 2. Bukhar, chai/coffee, ghabraahat ya khoon ki kami hai?; 3. Thyroid report normal hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Treat Underlying Cause + Propranolol / Metoprolol (if symptomatic)
Duration_Days: 7 to 14 days while treating primary cause
Supportive_Medicines: Anxiolytics short-term; Hydration; Iron supplements (if anemic)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Identify and treat underlying cause (Fever, Dehydration, Anemia, Hyperthyroidism, Anxiety, Infection); Beta blockers caution in bronchial asthma and COPD
Home_Care_Advice: Limit caffeine, tea, energy drinks, and nicotine; Practice deep breathing and relaxation; Hydrate well; Rest during fever
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG (sinus rhythm >100 bpm); Complete Blood Count; Thyroid Function Test (TSH); Serum Electrolytes
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Resting pulse >130 bpm without obvious cause; Chest pain; Syncope; High fever with shock

Primary_Symptoms: Regular slow heart rate (<60 bpm); Often asymptomatic in athletes; Fatigue; Dizziness
Secondary_Symptoms: Exertional dyspnea; Presyncope; Impaired concentration; Memory loss
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Heart rate 60 se kam rehta hai?; 2. Aap athlete hain ya koi BP/Heart ki dawai khaate hain?; 3. Chakkar ya behoshi hoti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Reassurance if asymptomatic OR Atropine (Emergency if symptomatic shock) / Permanent Pacemaker
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Atropine; Tab Cilacar (adjust beta blocker dose)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV in ER / Specialist management
Supportive_Medicines: Review and taper offending drugs (Beta blockers, Diltiazem, Digoxin); Pacemaker evaluation
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Physiological in trained athletes and during sleep; If symptomatic, urgently review beta blockers, verapamil, digoxin; Avoid self-medication
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid sudden standing; Review all current cardiac medications with doctor; Do not take OTC cold medicines containing beta blockers or sympatholytics
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG (sinus rhythm <60 bpm); 24-hour Holter Monitoring; Serum Electrolytes; Thyroid Function Test (rule out Hypothyroidism)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Heart rate <40 bpm with syncope/fainting; Confusion; Severe dizziness; Chest pain; Hypotension

Common_Names_Hindi: Heart Block; Dil ki wiring ki bimari
Primary_Symptoms: Delayed or blocked AV nodal conduction (1st, 2nd, or 3rd Degree); Dizziness; Syncope (Stokes-Adams attacks)
Secondary_Symptoms: Profound fatigue; Exertional dyspnea; Presyncope; Bradycardia (30-40 bpm); Confusion
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Heart beat bahut kam (30-40) aati hai?; 2. Behoshi (syncope) ke daure padte hain?; 3. ECG me Heart Block bataya hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Atropine / Isoprenaline acute, Permanent Pacemaker implant definitive)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV in ER under specialist
Supportive_Medicines: Temporary Transcutaneous/Transvenous Pacing; Permanent Dual-Chamber Pacemaker implantation
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; High risk of sudden cardiac death in Complete (3rd Degree) Heart Block; Strictly avoid beta blockers, verapamil, diltiazem, digoxin; Urgent cardiology admission
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid driving or operating machinery; Do not take any heart/BP meds without electrophysiologist clearance; Keep emergency contact ready
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG (P-R interval prolongation / AV dissociation); 24-hour Holter Monitor; Echocardiogram; Serum Electrolytes & Trop-I
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Syncope/Loss of consciousness; Heart rate <30 bpm; Severe breathlessness; Confusion

Common_Names_Hindi: Dhadkan mehsoos hona; Ghabraahat me dhadkan
Primary_Symptoms: Awareness of heart beating (fluttering/pounding) triggered by stress, caffeine, or anxiety; Normal heart structure
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild restlessness; Sweating; Hyperventilation; Sleep onset awareness; Absence of syncope
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dhadkan ghabraahat, chinta ya chai/coffee ke baad tez mehsoos hoti hai?; 2. ECG aur Echo report normal hain?; 3. Chakkar ya behoshi to nahi hui?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Propranolol OR Clonazepam (short-term low dose for anxiety)
Supportive_Medicines: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT); Relaxation exercises; Avoid stimulants
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Propranolol caution in bronchial asthma and severe hypoglycemia; Rule out organic cardiac arrhythmia/thyrotoxicosis before labeling benign
Home_Care_Advice: Stop caffeine, energy drinks, nicotine, and alcohol; Practice Pranayama and deep diaphragmatic breathing; Regular physical exercise
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG; Thyroid Function Test (TSH); Complete Blood Count (rule out anemia); 24-hour Holter (if frequent)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Palpitations associated with syncope, severe chest pain, or dyspnea; Irregular rapid pulse >150 bpm; Family history of sudden cardiac death

Primary_Symptoms: Sensation of a 'skipped beat' followed by a 'strong thump' in chest; Compensatory pause
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild anxiety; Neck fullness; Transient chest flutter; Lightheadedness (if frequent)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Lagta hai ki ek dhadkan miss ho kar tez dhak se aati hai?; 2. Caffeine ya stress me badhta hai?; 3. Daily routine me kitni baar hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Metoprolol OR Bisoprolol (Reassurance if asymptomatic & low burden <5%)
Supportive_Medicines: Potassium & Magnesium supplementation (if low); Radiofrequency Ablation (if burden >10-15% under specialist)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Asymptomatic PVCs in normal heart structure do NOT require aggressive antiarrhythmic drugs; Beta blockers caution in asthma
Home_Care_Advice: Reduce caffeine, alcohol, and stress; Ensure adequate sleep; Avoid sympathomimetic decongestants; Reassurance
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG (premature wide QRS without P wave); 24-hour Holter Monitor (quantify PVC burden %); Echocardiogram; Electrolytes
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Frequent multifocal PVCs; Runs of Ventricular Tachycardia (≥3 consecutive PVCs); Syncope; Structural heart disease co-existing

Primary_Symptoms: Transient sudden loss of consciousness with spontaneous complete recovery; Loss of postural tone
Secondary_Symptoms: Prodromal lightheadedness, nausea, diaphoresis, blurred vision (Vasovagal); Sudden fall without prodrome (Cardiac)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Behoshi se pehle chakkar, pasiina ya dhundla-pan aaya tha?; 2. Behoshi kitne second rehi aur apne aap hosh aaya?; 3. Khade hone par hua ya letne par?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Treat Specific Etiology (ORS/Salt for Vasovagal; Pacemaker for Cardiac Syncope)
Supportive_Medicines: Midodrine / Fludrocortisone (if neurocardiogenic syncope under specialist); Cardiac Pacemaker (if bradyarrhythmia)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rule out life-threatening cardiac causes (arrhythmia, aortic stenosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy) vs benign vasovagal syncope; Avoid driving until evaluated
Home_Care_Advice: If feeling faint, lie flat immediately with legs elevated; Avoid known triggers (prolonged standing, hot environment, blood draw); Hydrate liberally
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG (mandatory for all syncope); Echocardiogram; 24-48h Holter / Loop Recorder; Tilt Table Test; EEG & CT Brain (if seizure suspected)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Syncope during exertion or while supine; Syncope with chest pain or palpitations; Family history of sudden cardiac death; Head injury post fall

Primary_Symptoms: Exaggerated HR increase (≥30 bpm in adults) within 10 min of standing WITHOUT orthostatic hypotension; Dizziness
Secondary_Symptoms: Brain fog; Fatigue; Tremulousness; Palpitations on standing; Acrocyanosis (purple feet on standing)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khade hone ke 10 min me heart beat 30-40 badh jati hai par BP kam nahi hota?; 2. Khade rehne par chakkar aur thakan lagti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Propranolol (Low Dose) OR Ivabradine + Aggressive Salt/Fluid Intake
Supportive_Medicines: Abdominal binder; Waist-high compression stockings (20-30 mmHg); Midodrine 2.5 mg TDS
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; High-dose beta blockers worsen symptoms by accentuating fatigue and vasodilation; Propranolol caution in asthma
Home_Care_Advice: Drink 2.5-3 Liters of fluid daily; Increase salt intake (6-10g daily); Wear waist-high compression garments; Recumbent exercise training (rowing, swimming, recumbent bike)
Lab_Investigations: 10-minute Active Stand Test / Head-Up Tilt Table Test (HUTT); 24-hour Holter; Serum Electrolytes; Thyroid Profile
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Syncope with head injury; Severe incapacitating fatigue; Chest pain; Persistent pulse >150 bpm on standing

Common_Names_Hindi: Pairo ki nali me blockage; PAD
Primary_Symptoms: Intermittent claudication (cramping pain/fatigue in calf/thigh during walking, relieved by rest); Cold extremities
Secondary_Symptoms: Ischemic rest pain (foot pain at night relieved by dangling leg); Non-healing lower limb ulcers; Absent peripheral pulses; Hair loss on legs
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chalne par pairo (pindali) me tez dard/kramps hota hai jo rukne par teek hota hai?; 2. Pairo ki chhaal thandi rehti hai?; 3. Smoking/Diabetes hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Cilostazol + Aspirin + Atorvastatin
Supportive_Medicines: Clopidogrel 75 mg OD; Supervised Exercise Therapy; Pentoxifylline
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Cilostazol STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in Heart Failure of any severity (Black Box Warning); Aspirin GI bleeding caution; Statins caution in active liver disease
Home_Care_Advice: Complete smoking cessation mandatory; Supervised treadmill walking therapy (walk to pain threshold, rest, repeat); Daily inspection of feet for cuts/ulcers; Avoid tight socks
Lab_Investigations: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI <0.9 diagnostic); Arterial Doppler Ultrasound of lower limbs; CT / MR Angiography; Fasting Lipid & Glucose
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Critical Limb Ischemia (resting foot pain at night, gangrene/black toes, non-healing painful leg ulcers); Acute limb ischemia (6 Ps: Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, Paralysis, Poikilothermia)

Common_Names_Hindi: DVT Emergency; Pairo ki nas me khoon jamna
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden acute unilateral calf or thigh swelling, redness, warmth, and severe deep aching pain; Pitting edema
Secondary_Symptoms: Tenderness along deep veins (Homan's sign); Superficial venous dilation; Low fever; Pulmonary Embolism risk
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ek hi pair me achanak tez sujan, lalapan aur dard hua hai?; 2. Plaster, surgery, ya lambi yatra ke baad hua?; 3. Saans phoolti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Enoxaparin (LMWH); Tab Rivaroxaban 15; Tab Apixaban 5
Supportive_Medicines: Compression therapy post acute phase; Parenteral Enoxaparin / Heparin bridging
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency due to risk of fatal Pulmonary Embolism; Do NOT massage affected leg (can dislodge clot to lungs)
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to hospital; Keep affected leg elevated and resting motionless; Do NOT massage or rub swollen calf while transporting
Lab_Investigations: Venous Doppler Ultrasound of lower extremity (Gold standard); D-Dimer; CT Pulmonary Angiogram (if dyspnea present); PT/INR & APTT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; DVT with sudden breathlessness, chest pain, or hemoptysis (Pulmonary Embolism); Massive blue leg swelling (Phlegmasia Cerulea Dolens)

Primary_Symptoms: Tortuous, dilated, enlarged superficial veins in lower limbs; Heavy, aching leg discomfort after prolonged standing
Secondary_Symptoms: Pedal edema; Nocturnal leg cramps; Pruritus over veins; Hyperpigmentation (hemosiderin); Venous eczema
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pairo me neeli, moti, guchhe waali phooli nasein dikhti hain?; 2. Khade hone par pairo me bhari-pan aur dard badhta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Micronized Purified Flavonoid Fraction (MPFF - Diosmin + Hesperidin) OR Calcium Dobesilate
Supportive_Medicines: Class 2 Graduated Compression Stockings (20-30 mmHg); Endovenous Laser/Radiofrequency Ablation (EVLA/RFA under vascular surgeon)
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT wear compression stockings at night while sleeping; Compression stockings contraindicated in severe PAD (check ABI first)
Home_Care_Advice: Wear Class 2 compression stockings during daytime before getting out of bed; Elevate legs above heart level when resting; Avoid prolonged static standing/sitting
Lab_Investigations: Venous Doppler Ultrasound with Reflux Study (standing position); ABI measurement
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Sudden severe bleeding from a ruptured varicose vein (apply direct pressure and elevate leg); Superficial thrombophlebitis (painful red cord over vein); Non-healing venous ulcer

Common_Names_Hindi: Pairo me kharab circulation; Venous Insufficiency
Primary_Symptoms: Bilateral or unilateral lower leg edema; Hyperpigmentation (gaiter zone); Lipodermatosclerosis ('inverted bowling pin' leg)
Secondary_Symptoms: Venous stasis dermatitis; Pruritus; Shallow irregular non-healing venous ulcers near medial malleolus; Heavy legs
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ankles/pairo ke paas chamdi bhuri/kaali ho gayi hai aur sujan rehti hai?; 2. Sham ko pairo me dard-bhari lagta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Diosmin + Hesperidin (MPFF) OR Pentoxifylline + Compression Therapy
Supportive_Medicines: Unna boot paste bandage; Liquid paraffin emollient; Zinc oxide barrier cream; Wound dressings
Precautions_Contraindications: Compression therapy is cornerstone of treatment; Do NOT apply compression if ABI <0.8 (indicates co-existing arterial disease)
Home_Care_Advice: Elevate legs for 30 mins 3-4 times daily; Wear graduated compression stockings daily; Apply thick moisturizers to prevent stasis eczema cracking; Walk regularly
Lab_Investigations: Venous Doppler Ultrasound; Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI); Serum Albumin (rule out systemic edema)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Active infected venous ulcer with foul purulent discharge and surrounding cellulitis; Acute sudden calf swelling; Severe leg pain

Primary_Symptoms: Bilateral or unilateral swelling of feet, ankles, and lower legs; Pitting edema on thumb pressure
Secondary_Symptoms: Skin tightness; Weight gain; Heavy legs; Footwear feeling tight; Associated shortness of breath or oliguria
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dono pairo me sujan hai ya ek me?; 2. Angoothe se dabane par gaddha banta hai?; 3. Heart, Kidney, Liver ya BP ki dawai chal rahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Treat Underlying Cause + Furosemide OR Torsemide (if fluid overload present)
Supportive_Medicines: Compression stockings (if venous); Salt restriction; Potassium supplements (if loop diuretic used)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Diuretics require potassium, creatinine, and hydration monitoring; Avoid overuse causing prerenal acute kidney injury; Amlodipine/Cilnidipine often cause drug-induced pedal edema
Home_Care_Advice: Elevate feet on pillows while sitting/sleeping; Restrict salt intake (<3-5g/day); Avoid standing still for long hours; Review medications with doctor
Lab_Investigations: Serum Creatinine, Blood Urea, Electrolytes; LFT & Serum Albumin; Echocardiogram; Urine Routine/Protein; Thyroid Profile (TSH)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Sudden unilateral painful leg swelling (DVT rule out); Swelling accompanied by acute breathlessness (pulmonary edema); Severe oliguria

Primary_Symptoms: Reversible digital vasospasm triggered by cold/stress: Triphasic color change (Pallor/White -> Cyanosis/Blue -> Erythema/Red)
Secondary_Symptoms: Digital numbness; Tingling; Burning pain during rewarming; Digital tip ulcers (secondary Raynaud's)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Thand me haath/pair ki ungliya pehle safed, fir neeli, aur fir lal ho jati hain?; 2. Ungliyo me sunn-pan aur dard hota hai?; 3. Joint pain ya skin tight hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Nifedipine (Sustained Release) OR Amlodipine
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Nitroglycerin 0.2% ointment; Sildenafil 25 mg BD (for severe digital ulcers under specialist); Hand warmers
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Nifedipine caution in hypotension and heart failure; Avoid Beta blockers (they trigger vasospasm)
Home_Care_Advice: Keep hands and body warm (wear thick insulated gloves and woollen socks); Avoid cold water and ice; Complete smoking cessation; Avoid sympathomimetic nasal sprays
Lab_Investigations: ANA (Antinuclear Antibodies by IFA - rule out Systemic Sclerosis/Lupus); Nailfold Capillaroscopy; ESR/CRP; CBC
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Digital tip necrosis or blackening (gangrene); Non-healing painful digital ulcers; Persistent unilateral digit color change

Primary_Symptoms: Systemic lipid plaque accumulation in arteries; Asymptomatic early; Causes angina, claudication, or TIA as plaque grows
Secondary_Symptoms: Reduced arterial pulses; Vascular bruits; Fatigue; Ischemic symptoms in heart, brain, or legs
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Cholesterol/Lipid report me kitna bada aaya hai?; 2. Diabetes, High BP, ya Smoking ki history hai?; 3. Chhati me dard ya chalne me pairo me dard hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Atorvastatin OR Rosuvastatin + Aspirin (if vascular disease established)
Supportive_Medicines: Ezetimibe 10 mg OD (added if LDL target not met); Anti-hypertensives; Anti-diabetic agents
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Statins contraindicated in pregnancy and active liver disease; Monitor baseline Liver Function Tests; Advise reporting unexplained muscle pain (rhabdomyolysis risk)
Home_Care_Advice: Strict low-saturated-fat and low-cholesterol diet; 150 mins/week moderate exercise; Complete smoking/tobacco cessation; Strict BP and sugar control
Lab_Investigations: Fasting Lipid Profile (Target LDL <70 mg/dL or <55 mg/dL if high risk); Fasting Glucose & HbA1c; LFT; Carotid Doppler / ABI
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Symptoms of acute arterial occlusion: chest pain (MI), focal weakness/slurred speech (Stroke), or sudden cold painful limb (Acute Limb Ischemia)

Primary_Symptoms: Atherosclerotic narrowing of carotid arteries; Often asymptomatic; Discovered by neck bruit or post-TIA/Stroke
Secondary_Symptoms: Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA): amaurosis fugax (monocular vision loss), unilateral weakness, dysarthria
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Gardan ki nali (Carotid) me blockage bataya hai?; 2. Achanak ek taraf ki weakness, bolne me takleef, ya aankh ke aage andhera aaya tha?; 3. Ultrasound hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Atorvastatin + Aspirin + Clopidogrel
Supportive_Medicines: Carotid Endarterectomy (CEA) / Carotid Artery Stenting (CAS) if stenosis >70% symptomatic or >80% asymptomatic
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Statins require LFT monitoring; Dual antiplatelets require monitoring for GI bleeding and bruising; Avoid blood pressure drops
Home_Care_Advice: Strict control of BP (<130/80) and Diabetes; Zero tobacco use; Mediterranean diet; Regular follow-up carotid Doppler imaging
Lab_Investigations: Carotid Doppler Ultrasound; CT Angiography of Head and Neck; MRI Brain; Fasting Lipid Profile; HbA1c
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) signs: sudden weakness on one side of body, facial drooping, speech difficulty, or sudden monocular blindness

Primary_Symptoms: Elevated Low-Density Lipoprotein (LDL-C >130-160 mg/dL); Asymptomatic; Tendon xanthomas (in familial types)
Secondary_Symptoms: Arcus senilis; Xanthelasma around eyes; Increased risk of CAD and Stroke
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Fasting lipid report me LDL (Bad Cholesterol) kitna hai?; 2. Family me Heart Attack ya High Cholesterol ki history hai?; 3. BP ya Diabetes hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Atorvastatin OR Rosuvastatin
Supportive_Medicines: Ezetimibe 10 mg OD; Fiber supplements (Psyllium husk); Low-fat diet
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Statins strictly CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy, lactating mothers, and active liver disease; Check baseline LFT; Report unexplained muscle pain/weakness immediately
Home_Care_Advice: Switch to low-saturated-fat, trans-fat-free diet; Increase soluble fiber (oats, legumes, psyllium); 30-45 mins daily aerobic exercise; Stop smoking
Lab_Investigations: Fasting Lipid Profile (Total Cholesterol, LDL, HDL, Triglycerides); LFT (ALT/AST); Fasting Blood Glucose; TSH (rule out secondary hypothyroidism)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Unexplained severe muscle pain or dark tea-colored urine (rhabdomyolysis); Chest pain; Focal neurological deficits

Common_Names_Hindi: High Triglycerides; High Fat in Blood
Primary_Symptoms: Elevated Serum Triglycerides (>150-200 mg/dL; Severe >500 mg/dL); Asymptomatic; Eruptive xanthomas (if >1000 mg/dL)
Secondary_Symptoms: Lipemia retinalis; Hepatosplenomegaly; Acute Pancreatitis risk (when TG >500-1000 mg/dL)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Fasting lipid report me Triglycerides kitne hain (>200 ya >500)?; 2. Alcohol, sweets, ya oily food zyada khate hain?; 3. Pet me tez dard to nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Fenofibrate OR Ethyl Icosapentate (Omega-3 fatty acids)
Supportive_Medicines: Atorvastatin (if combined high LDL); Strict low-carb, zero-alcohol diet
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Fenofibrate caution in severe renal impairment (eGFR <30) and gallbladder disease; Risk of myopathy increases when combined with statins
Home_Care_Advice: STRICT ZERO ALCOHOL; Eliminate refined sugars, sweets, fruit juices, and refined carbs; Low-fat diet; Weight loss; Exercise daily
Lab_Investigations: Fasting Lipid Profile; Serum Lipase & Amylase (if TG >500 mg/dL to rule out Pancreatitis); HbA1c; LFT; RFT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe continuous epigastric pain radiating to back with vomiting (Acute Pancreatitis triggered by hypertriglyceridemia >500-1000 mg/dL)

Primary_Symptoms: Co-existing elevated LDL-C (>130 mg/dL) and Triglycerides (>200 mg/dL) with Low HDL-C (<40 mg/dL); Asymptomatic
Secondary_Symptoms: Accelerated atherosclerosis risk; Metabolic syndrome association; Xanthelasma
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Lipid profile me Cholesterol aur Triglycerides dono bade hue hain?; 2. Fatty liver, Diabetes, ya overweight hai?; 3. BP bada hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rosuvastatin + Fenofibrate OR Atorvastatin + Ezetimibe
Supportive_Medicines: Saroglitazar 4 mg OD (Dual PPAR alpha/gamma agonist); Low-fat, low-carb diet
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Statin + Fibrinate combination increases myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk; Monitor LFT and Creatine Kinase (CK); Contraindicated in active liver/gallbladder disease and severe CKD
Home_Care_Advice: Combined dietary restriction: low saturated fats, zero trans-fats, zero refined sugars, and zero alcohol; 150 mins/week exercise; Weight reduction
Lab_Investigations: Fasting Lipid Profile; LFT (baseline and 3-month); Serum Creatinine; Creatine Kinase (if muscle pain occurs); Fasting Glucose & HbA1c
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness with dark brownish urine; Severe abdominal pain; Jaundice

Primary_Symptoms: Extreme elevation of LDL-C (>190 mg/dL in adults, >160 in children) from birth; Tendon xanthomas (Achilles/hands); Arcenia
Secondary_Symptoms: Xanthelasma; Premature Coronary Artery Disease (<50 years in men, <60 in women); Angina
Clarifying_Questions: 1. LDL Cholesterol 190 se bahut zyada hai?; 2. Family me kam umar me Heart Attack ya high cholesterol ki history hai?; 3. Achilles tendon par gummda hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (High-intensity Statin + Ezetimibe + PCSK9 Inhibitors)
Supportive_Medicines: Bempedoic Acid 180 mg OD; Bile acid sequestrants; Lipoprotein Apheresis
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; High 20-fold risk of premature heart attack; Monotherapy insufficient; Requires combination therapy; Statins strictly contraindicated in pregnancy; Regular LFT monitoring
Home_Care_Advice: Strict lifelong low-cholesterol diet; Early screening of all first-degree family members (cascade screening); Zero smoking; Complete vascular risk control
Lab_Investigations: Fasting Lipid Panel (LDL-C quantification); Genetic testing for LDLR, APOB, PCSK9 mutations; LFT; Lipoprotein(a); Cardiac CT / TMT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Any chest pain, tightness, or exertional dyspnea in a young patient with FH; Tendon pain/rupture; Jaundice

Common_Names_Hindi: Heart ka valve dheela hona; MVP
Primary_Symptoms: Systolic click and late systolic murmur on auscultation; Often asymptomatic; Mid-chest atypical pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Palpitations; Lightheadedness; Anxiety; Fatigue; Dyspnea; Panic attacks
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Echo test me Mitral Valve Prolapse (MVP) aaya hai?; 2. Chhati me dhak-dhak ya halka dard hota hai?; 3. Ghabraahat hoti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Reassurance + Metoprolol OR Propranolol (if symptomatic palpitations)
Supportive_Medicines: Anxiolytics short-term; Hydration; Antibiotic prophylaxis NO LONGER routinely required for dental work
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Reassure patient regarding excellent long-term prognosis in uncomplicated MVP; Beta blockers caution in asthma
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid excess caffeine, alcohol, and dehydration; Regular low-impact aerobic exercise; Reassurance regarding benign nature
Lab_Investigations: Echocardiography with Doppler (assess degree of mitral regurgitation and leaflet displacement); 12-lead ECG; Holter monitor (if palpitations present)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Sudden onset severe dyspnea, orthopnea, or hemoptysis (acute severe mitral regurgitation); Syncope; Infective endocarditis signs (fever + new murmur)

Common_Names_Hindi: Heart ki nali ka sikudna; Aortic Stenosis
Primary_Symptoms: Classic Triad: Exertional Dyspnea, Angina Pectoris, and Syncope; Crescendo-decrescendo systolic ejection murmur
Secondary_Symptoms: Fatigue; Heart Failure signs; Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea; Weak delayed carotid pulse (Pulsus parvus et tardus)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Heart ka Aortic Valve sikuda hua (stenosis) bataya hai?; 2. Chalne par saans phoolti hai, chhati me dard hota hai, ya chakkar aakar behoshi hui hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement - SAVR / TAVI; Medical bridging)
Duration_Days: Rx - specialist supervision required (Until surgical replacement)
Supportive_Medicines: Cautious low-dose diuretics for congestion; Avoid aggressive vasodilation; TAVI / SAVR evaluation
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; ONCE SYMPTOMATIC, AORTIC STENOSIS HAS HIGH MORTALITY WITHOUT VALVE REPLACEMENT; Nitrates, ACE inhibitors, and PDE5 inhibitors strictly contraindicated or used with extreme caution (cause fatal hypotension)
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid strenuous physical exertion or heavy weightlifting; Report any syncopal episodes immediately; Regular cardiological follow-up
Lab_Investigations: Echocardiogram with Doppler (Aortic Valve Area <1.0 cm², Mean Gradient >40 mmHg = Severe AS); Cardiac Catheterization; ECG; Chest X-ray
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency referral; Any syncopal episode; Angina at rest; Acute pulmonary edema (severe breathlessness); Heart failure progression

Primary_Symptoms: History of Rheumatic Fever; Valvular damage (Mitral Stenosis/Regurgitation); Dyspnea; Murmurs
Secondary_Symptoms: Fatigue; Palpitations; Joint pain history; Chorea history; Thromboembolism risk
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Bachpan me joints me dard aur Rheumatic fever hua tha?; 2. Heart valve me kharabi hai?; 3. Sui (Penicillin injection) har 3-4 hafte me lagti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Benzathine Penicillin G (Intramuscular Injection every 3-4 weeks) OR Oral Erythromycin / Azithromycin (if Penicillin allergic)
Dosage_Frequency: Every 3 to 4 weeks deep IM injection / OD (Azithromycin)
Duration_Days: Lifelong or up to age 25-40 per guideline severity
Supportive_Medicines: Oral Penicillin V 250 mg BD alternative; Diuretics and Warfarin if AF/Mitral Stenosis present
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; MANDATORY SKIN TEST (AST) BEFORE EVERY BENZATHINE PENICILLIN INJECTION due to fatal anaphylaxis risk; Complete strict adherence to 3-4 weekly schedule
Home_Care_Advice: Strict adherence to 21-28 day injection schedule without missing doses; Maintain good dental hygiene to prevent Infective Endocarditis
Lab_Investigations: Echocardiography (assess valve area and regurgitation); ASO Titer; ECG; INR (if on Warfarin for AF)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Anaphylactic shock signs post injection (stridor, collapse); Sudden breathlessness, hemoptysis, or stroke signs; Fever with new murmur

Primary_Symptoms: High persistent fever with chills; New or changing heart murmur; Splinter hemorrhages under nails; Roth spots
Secondary_Symptoms: Janeway lesions (painless palmar macules); Osler nodes (painful finger nodules); Embolic stroke; Hematuria; Fatigue
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Fasting me high fever aur heart me naya murmur bataya hai?; 2. Naakhun ke niche kaali dharaiya ya haath par lal daag hain?; 3. Valve surgery hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Ceftriaxone 2g IV; Injection Ampicillin; Injection Gentamicin
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV emergency administration in hospital
Supportive_Medicines: High-dose IV bactericidal Antibiotics for 4-6 weeks; Emergency Valve Surgery evaluation if refractory/heart failure
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT give home oral antibiotics or antipyretics without blood cultures; Immediate hospital admission required
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate transfer to tertiary hospital with cardiology and cardiac surgery ICU; Rest in bed; Do not attempt self-medication
Lab_Investigations: Blood Cultures x 3 sets (prior to initiating antibiotics); Transesophageal Echocardiogram (TEE - detect vegetations/abscess); CBC; ESR/CRP; Urine Routine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; High fever with embolic stroke, severe breathlessness, acute valve regurgitation, or heart failure

Common_Names_Hindi: Heart ki patti me sujan; Pericarditis
Primary_Symptoms: Sharp retrosternal pleuritic chest pain aggravated by inspiration/supine position and RELIEVED BY LEANING FORWARD
Secondary_Symptoms: Pericardial friction rub; Low grade fever; Dyspnea; Trapezius ridge pain radiation; Tachycardia
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chhati me tez dard letne par aur saans lene par badhta hai?; 2. Aage jhuk kar baithne par dard me aaram milta hai?; 3. Post-viral bukhar hua tha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Colchicine + Ibuprofen OR Indomethacin
Duration_Days: 14 to 28 days (Ibuprofen) / 3 months (Colchicine to prevent recurrence)
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD (gastric protection); Paracetamol 650 mg SOS
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Colchicine dose reduction in renal impairment; NSAIDs contraindicated in active peptic ulcer, severe CKD, and post-MI pericarditis; Avoid Aspirin if on anticoagulants
Home_Care_Advice: Rest until symptoms and inflammatory markers normalize; Avoid strenuous physical exercise or sports for at least 3 months; Take meds strictly with food
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG (widespread diffuse ST elevation with PR depression); Echocardiogram (check pericardial effusion); CRP/ESR; Troponin-I
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Beck's Triad of Cardiac Tamponade: Hypotension, Distended neck veins, and Muffled heart sounds; Severe acute dyspnea; Paradoxical pulse

Common_Names_Hindi: Heart ki manspeshi ki sujan; Myocarditis
Primary_Symptoms: Acute onset retrosternal chest pain, dyspnea at rest, and fatigue following a viral febrile illness; Arrhythmias
Secondary_Symptoms: Heart Failure signs; Tachycardia out of proportion to fever; Syncope; Sudden cardiogenic shock; Fever
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Viral bukhar ke baad chhati me dard, saans phoolna aur tez dhadkan hui hai?; 2. Fatigue itna hai ki chala nahi jata?; 3. Behoshi hui hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Hydrocortisone; Tab Sacubitril/Valsartan; Tab Metoprolol
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV and ICU supportive care in hospital
Supportive_Medicines: ICU monitoring; Inotropic/Vasopressor support; Mechanical Circulatory Support (ECMO/IABP); Heart Failure meds once stable
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT attempt exercise or home treatment; High risk of fatal ventricular arrhythmias and fulminant shock
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to cardiac ICU hospital; Absolute physical bed rest; Avoid any physical exertion while transporting
Lab_Investigations: Cardiac Troponin-I / Troponin-T (significantly elevated); 12-lead ECG; Echocardiogram; Cardiac MRI (Gold standard non-invasive); Viral PCR panel
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Fulminant cardiogenic shock; Severe acute dyspnea; Ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation; Syncope

Primary_Symptoms: Structural and functional abnormality of myocardium (Dilated / Hypertrophic / Restrictive); Exertional dyspnea
Secondary_Symptoms: Pedal edema; Palpitations; Syncope; Orthopnea; Angina; Sudden cardiac death risk (in HCM)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Heart ki manspeshi phooli hui (Dilated) ya moti (Hypertrophic) batayi hai?; 2. Saans phoolti hai ya chakkar/behoshi aati hai?; 3. Family history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy - Sacubitril/Valsartan / Metoprolol / Mavacamten)
Supportive_Medicines: Spironolactone 25 mg OD; Dapagliflozin 10 mg OD; Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator (ICD) evaluation
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; High risk of sudden cardiac death in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM); Avoid strenuous competitive sports; Avoid dehydration and aggressive diuresis in HCM
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid intense competitive athletic training or heavy weightlifting; Daily weight monitoring; Low-salt diet; Family genetic screening
Lab_Investigations: Echocardiography with Doppler & Strain imaging; Cardiac MRI; 24-48h Holter Monitoring; Genetic Testing Panel; NT-proBNP
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Syncope or near-syncope (especially in HCM); Severe acute respiratory distress; Sustained palpitations; Sudden leg edema surge

Common_Names_Hindi: Phephde ki nali me High BP; PAH
Primary_Symptoms: Progressive exertional dyspnea; Severe fatigue; Exertional chest pain; Presyncope/Syncope on exertion
Secondary_Symptoms: Right heart failure signs: jugular venous distension, hepatomegaly, ascites, bilateral pedal edema; Loud P2 sound
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Phephde ki nali ka BP (Pulmonary Artery Pressure) bada hua hai?; 2. Thoda sa chalne par severe saans phoolti hai aur chakkar aate hain?; 3. Pairo me sujan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Endothelin Receptor Antagonists - Ambrisentan / Sildenafil / Treprostinil)
Supportive_Medicines: Diuretics (Furosemide); Anticoagulation (in CTEPH); Oxygen therapy; Digoxin
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Ambrisentan is STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy (highly teratogenic); Liver function monitoring mandatory for ERAs; Avoid pregnancy strictly
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid pregnancy strictly (high maternal mortality); Continuous supplemental oxygen if hypoxemic; Avoid high altitude; Gentle low-impact physical activity only
Lab_Investigations: Right Heart Catheterization (Gold standard - Mean PAP >20 mmHg at rest); Echocardiogram; CT Pulmonary Angiography; 6-Minute Walk Test
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Syncope during low-level exertion; Right heart failure decompensation (worsening ascites, leg edema, jaundice); Acute breathlessness; Hemoptysis

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden onset excruciating, tearing or ripping chest pain radiating to back between shoulder blades; Collapse
Secondary_Symptoms: Pulse deficit (asymmetric pulses in arms); Neurological deficits (stroke-like); Hypotension or Severe HTN; Aortic regurgitation
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chhati me achanak phatne (tearing/ripping) jaisa severe dard hua hai jo peth tak ja raha hai?; 2. Dono haath ka BP alag aata hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Labetalol IV; Injection Sodium Nitroprusside; Injection Morphine
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV BP and HR reduction in ICU
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate Surgical Repair (Type A) or Endovascular Stent Grafting (TEVAR - Type B); IV Labetalol to HR <60 and SBP <120
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Catastrophic emergency with 1-2% mortality per hour if untreated; Thrombolytics and anticoagulants strictly CONTRAINDICATED (causes fatal rupture)
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to tertiary cardiothoracic surgical center; Keep patient absolute still and flat; Do NOT give Aspirin or blood thinners
Lab_Investigations: Contrast-Enhanced CT Angiography of Chest and Abdomen (Gold standard); Transesophageal Echocardiogram (TEE); 12-lead ECG; ABG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Tearing chest/back pain; Asymmetric blood pressure/pulses; Stroke symptoms with chest pain; Syncope

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden onset FAST signs: Facial drooping, Arm weakness/numbness, Speech difficulty; Loss of balance; Vision loss
Secondary_Symptoms: Sudden severe thunderclap headache; Confusion; Dizziness; Loss of consciousness; Vomiting; Dysphagia
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Achanak muuh terha hua, haath me kamzori aayi, ya bolne me takleef hui hai?; 2. Ye kitne baje/ghante pehle shuru hua?; 3. Behoshi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Alteplase (tPA); Tab Clopidogrel 75; Tab Atorvastatin 40
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency IV thrombolysis within 4.5h window in stroke center
Supportive_Medicines: Intravenous Thrombolysis (tPA within 4.5 hours); Mechanical Thrombectomy (within 24 hours); Airway protection; BP management
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; DO NOT GIVE ASPIRIN OR ANY MEDICINE BEFORE BRAIN IMAGING (must rule out Hemorrhagic Stroke first); Note exact time symptoms started
Home_Care_Advice: Call emergency stroke ambulance immediately; Note exact time symptoms started; Keep patient resting on side if vomiting; DO NOT give any food, water, or oral medicine
Lab_Investigations: Non-Contrast CT Brain (immediate - rule out bleed); MRI Brain (DWI); CT Angiography Head & Neck; Blood Glucose (rule out hypoglycemia); PT/INR
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Any FAST stroke signs; Sudden loss of consciousness; Seizures with weakness; Severe sudden headache

Common_Names_Hindi: A-cardiac Chhati me dard; Non-cardiac Pain
Primary_Symptoms: Chest wall or retrosternal pain that is localized, sharp, positional, or reproducible on palpation; Normal ECG/Troponin
Secondary_Symptoms: Relation to meals or swallowing (GERD/Esophageal); Relation to respiration/movement (Musculoskeletal); Absence of radiation
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chhati me dard dabane, saans lene, ya mudne par badhta hai?; 2. Khana khane ya acidity se sambandh hai?; 3. ECG report normal aayi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pantoprazole (if GERD) OR Paracetamol / Cyclobenzaprine (if Musculoskeletal)
Supportive_Medicines: Antacid gel; Local warm compress / Volini gel; Reassurance after ruling out cardiac origin
Precautions_Contraindications: MUST RULE OUT ISCHEMIC HEART DISEASE (CAD/ACS) BEFORE DIAGNOSING NON-CARDIAC PAIN; NSAIDs caution in peptic ulcer; Paracetamol safe for musculoskeletal chest pain
Home_Care_Advice: Apply local warm compress for muscle pain; Take small, bland, non-spicy meals if acid reflux related; Avoid heavy lifting; Reassurance
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG (mandatory to rule out ischemia); Troponin-I; Chest X-ray; Upper GI Endoscopy (if reflux suspected)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Pain changing character to severe retrosternal pressure/crushing sensation with sweating; Pain radiating to left arm/jaw; Dyspnea

Primary_Symptoms: Sharp, fleeting or persistent precordial chest pain associated with overt anxiety, panic, hyperventilation, and normal cardiac tests
Secondary_Symptoms: Palpitations; Circumoral paresthesia; Tremors; Feeling of choking; Normal exercise tolerance; Normal ECG
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chhati me dard ghabraahat, chinta ya panic attack ke waqt hota hai?; 2. Sabhi heart reports (ECG, Echo, TMT) normal hain?; 3. Haath-pairo me chiintiya kat ti hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Reassurance + Clonazepam OR Escitalopram (if underlying Panic Disorder)
Supportive_Medicines: Propranolol 10 mg SOS for somatic palpitations; Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT); Breathing exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Benzodiazepines (Clonazepam) carry dependency risk - restrict to short-term SOS use; Rule out organic cardiac disease first; Avoid abrupt discontinuation
Home_Care_Advice: Practice diaphragmatic 4-7-8 breathing during attack; Reassure self that heart is medically normal; Reduce caffeine and alcohol; Regular exercise and yoga
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG; Treadmill Stress Test (TMT - reassuring); Echocardiogram; Thyroid Function Test; Complete Blood Count
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; New atypical pain radiating to arm/jaw; Syncope; True exertional angina; Persistent panic attacks non-responsive to therapy

Common_Names_Hindi: High BP se Aankh ki bimari
Primary_Symptoms: Progressive microvascular retinal changes secondary to chronic HTN; Asymptomatic early; Blurring of vision in late stages
Secondary_Symptoms: Arteriolar narrowing; AV nicking; Cotton wool spots; Flame hemorrhages; Papilledema (in malignant HTN)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. High BP kitne saal se hai?; 2. Fundus / Aankh ki janch hui hai?; 3. Dhundla-pan ya roshni kam hui hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Strict BP Control with Telmisartan / Amlodipine + Ophthalmic Monitoring
Supportive_Medicines: Laser photocoagulation / Anti-VEGF intravitreal injections (if severe macular edema under ophthalmologist)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Target BP <130/80 mm Hg to prevent progression; Avoid sudden extreme BP drops in chronic malignant HTN
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain strict daily BP control; Take antihypertensive meds without fail; Annual dilated fundus examination by ophthalmologist; Control diabetes and lipids
Lab_Investigations: Dilated Fundoscopic Examination (Scheie / Keith-Wagener-Barker classification); Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT); BP Logbook
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Sudden loss of vision or severe blurring; Papilledema on fundoscopy; Hypertensive crisis (BP >180/120 mm Hg)

Primary_Symptoms: Asymptomatic early; Classic Triad: Polyuria (frequent urination), Polydipsia (excessive thirst), Polyphagia (excessive hunger)
Secondary_Symptoms: Unexplained weight loss; Fatigue; Blurred vision; Slow wound healing; Recurrent fungal/urinary infections
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Fasting sugar >126 mg/dL ya HbA1c >6.5% hai?; 2. Baar-baar peshab aur pyas lagti hai?; 3. Family history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Metformin
Dosage_Frequency: BD (12 hourly with or after meals)
Supportive_Medicines: Teneligliptin 20 mg OD / Empagliflozin 10 mg OD; Multivitamins with B-complex; Diabetic diet
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Metformin contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min), acute dehydration, and before IV contrast dye; Long-term use requires Vitamin B12 monitoring; Avoid alcohol (lactic acidosis risk)
Home_Care_Advice: Follow strict low-glycemic-index diabetic diet (no sweets, refined carbs, sugary drinks); 150 mins/week exercise; Daily foot inspection; Maintain normal weight
Lab_Investigations: HbA1c (every 3 months, target <7.0%); Fasting & Postprandial Blood Glucose; Serum Creatinine & eGFR; Urinary Microalbumin; Lipid Profile
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Hypoglycemia signs (sweating, tremors, confusion); Fasting sugar >250 mg/dL or HbA1c >10%; Non-healing foot ulcer; Ketone breath odor

Primary_Symptoms: Asymptomatic; Impaired Fasting Glucose (100-125 mg/dL) or Impaired Glucose Tolerance (140-199 mg/dL 2h post-glucose); HbA1c 5.7-6.4%
Secondary_Symptoms: Acanthosis nigricans (dark velvety neck folds); Central obesity; Fatigue post meals; Metabolic syndrome
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Fasting sugar 100-125 ke beech hai ya HbA1c 5.7-6.4% hai?; 2. Weight ya pet ki charbi zyada hai?; 3. Gardan par kaala-pan (acanthosis) hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Lifestyle Modification First-Line OR Metformin (if high risk / BMI >35 / age <60)
Supportive_Medicines: B-complex vitamins; Fiber supplements; Weight loss program
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Primary therapy is intensive lifestyle intervention; Metformin used off-label/guideline for high-risk prediabetes; Monitor renal function and B12 on Metformin
Home_Care_Advice: Aim for 7% body weight loss; 150 mins/week moderate aerobic exercise (brisk walking); Eliminate refined sugars, bakery items, and sodas; Eat high fiber diet
Lab_Investigations: HbA1c (every 6 months); Fasting Blood Glucose & 75g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT); Lipid Profile; LFT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Fasting sugar rising >126 mg/dL or HbA1c ≥6.5% (progression to frank Diabetes); Onset of classic diabetic symptoms (polyuria/polydipsia)

Common_Names_Hindi: Insulin Resistance; Sugar hone ki pehli stage
Primary_Symptoms: Asymptomatic elevated fasting insulin levels; Acanthosis nigricans (dark velvety skin folds on neck, axillae); Abdominal obesity
Secondary_Symptoms: Fatigue post high-carb meals; Carbohydrate cravings; Difficulty losing weight; Irregular periods (in females with PCOS)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Gardan ya bagal par kaali velvety patti (acanthosis) hai?; 2. Khana khane ke baad zyada neend aur thakan aati hai?; 3. Weight loss nahi ho raha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Metformin (Off-label for Insulin Sensitization) + Lifestyle Modification
Supportive_Medicines: Myo-Inositol 2g BD (if co-existing PCOS); Alpha-Lipoic Acid; Chromium picolinate
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Primary management is dietary and exercise interventions; Metformin requires B12 monitoring; Contraindicated in severe kidney failure
Home_Care_Advice: Adopt Low-Carbohydrate / Low-GI diet; Intermittent fasting or structured meal timing; Strength training + Aerobic exercise; Eliminate refined sugar and processed foods
Lab_Investigations: Fasting Insulin & Fasting Glucose (calculate HOMA-IR index >2.5); HbA1c; Lipid Profile; USG Pelvis (if PCOS suspected)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Fasting glucose rising >100-126 mg/dL; Development of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome symptoms; Unexplained weight changes

Primary_Symptoms: Classic Triad: Polyuria, Polydipsia, Polyphagia with RAPID UNEXPLAINED WEIGHT LOSS in children/young adults; Diabetic Ketoacidosis
Secondary_Symptoms: Fatigue; Lethargy; Blurred vision; Abdominal pain; Vomiting; Fruity breath odor; Kussmaul breathing
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sugar jawani/bachpan me shuru hui hai?; 2. Achanak weight bohut kam hua hai?; 3. Subah aur khane se pehle Insulin ke injection lagte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Basal-Bolus Subcutaneous Insulin Regimen)
Adult_Strength_Mg: Units per kg (Individualized by Endocrinologist strictly)
Dosage_Frequency: Subcutaneous injections multiple times daily (Basal once daily + Bolus before meals)
Meal_Timing: 15 min Before Meals (Rapid insulin) / Fixed time at bedtime (Basal)
Supportive_Medicines: Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM); Flash Glucose Monitor; Fast-acting Glucose tablets SOS for hypoglycemia
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; NEVER STOP INSULIN IN TYPE 1 DIABETES (stopping causes fatal Diabetic Ketoacidosis); High risk of Hypoglycemia - carry fast-acting sugar always; Doses strictly individualized by doctor
Home_Care_Advice: Self-Monitoring of Blood Glucose (SMBG) 4-6 times daily; Count carbohydrates for insulin bolus matching; Rotate insulin injection sites; Always carry 15g fast-acting glucose
Lab_Investigations: HbA1c (every 3 months); Continuous Glucose Monitor log; Anti-GAD & IA-2 Antibodies; C-Peptide level; Urine Ketones; Annual Complication Screening
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency referral; Blood glucose >250 mg/dL with urine ketones / fruity breath (Diabetic Ketoacidosis); Severe Hypoglycemia (<50 mg/dL) with confusion

Primary_Symptoms: Hyperglycemia first recognized during pregnancy (Fasting ≥92 mg/dL, 1h ≥180, 2h ≥153 on 75g OGTT); Usually asymptomatic
Secondary_Symptoms: Excessive fetal growth (Macrosomia); Polyhydramnios; Fatigue; Recurrent vaginal candidiasis
Typical_Duration: Duration of pregnancy (usually resolves post delivery)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pregnancy ke dauran sugar nikli hai?; 2. Fasting ya khane ke baad ki sugar report me kitni hai?; 3. Ultrasound me baby ka weight/paani zyada hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Dietary Therapy First-Line; Insulin Subcutaneous / Metformin under Specialist)
Adult_Strength_Mg: Units / mg individualized strictly by Specialist
Dosage_Frequency: Subcutaneous Insulin before meals/bedtime OR Metformin BD
Supportive_Medicines: Self-Monitoring of Blood Glucose (SMBG) logbook; Prenatal Vitamins; Folic Acid 5 mg
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Strict glycemic targets in GDM (Fasting <95 mg/dL, 1h postprandial <140, 2h <120); Most oral anti-diabetics contraindicated in pregnancy except Metformin under specialist guidance
Home_Care_Advice: Strict GDM meal planning (carbohydrate distribution across 3 main meals and 3 snacks); Daily SMBG testing 4 times/day; Gentle 15-min post-meal walking
Lab_Investigations: 75g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT - DIPSI criteria); SMBG Logbook; HbA1c; Fetal Growth USG with Doppler
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Fasting glucose persistently >95 mg/dL or postprandial >140 mg/dL despite diet; Hypoglycemia; Decreased fetal movements; Pre-eclampsia signs

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden Blood Glucose <70 mg/dL: Tremors, Diaphoresis (cold sweat), Tachycardia, Anxiety, Hunger, Palpitations
Secondary_Symptoms: Neuroglycopenic symptoms: Confusion, Dizziness, Slurred speech, Blurred vision, Seizures, Coma
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Blood Sugar 70 se kam aayi hai?; 2. Pasiina, kapaahat, chakkar, aur bhookh achanak hui hai?; 3. Insulin ya Sugar ki dawai chal rahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: 15 g Fast-Acting Sugar (First Aid) / Glucagon IM or 25% Dextrose IV (if unconscious in ER)
Adult_Strength_Mg: 15 g Fast-Acting Glucose (e.g., 3 teaspoons sugar or glucose in water)
Supportive_Medicines: Follow with a complex carbohydrate snack (chapati/biscuit/milk) once sugar recovers >70 mg/dL
Precautions_Contraindications: Rule of 15: Take 15g fast-acting sugar, wait 15 mins, recheck sugar. If still <70, repeat 15g sugar; DO NOT GIVE FOOD OR DRINK TO AN UNCONSCIOUS PERSON (aspiration risk); Sulfonylureas (Glimepiride) cause prolonged hypoglycemia
Home_Care_Advice: Always carry glucose tablets, sugar pouches, or candy if on insulin/sulfonylureas; Educate family members on hypoglycemia recognition and handling; Re-evaluate diabetes drug doses with doctor
Lab_Investigations: Capillary Blood Glucose (Glucometer check immediately); Serum Glucose; HbA1c review; Sulfonylurea level (if suspected overdose)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Unconsciousness, seizures, or inability to swallow (Call emergency ambulance for IV Dextrose / IM Glucagon); Hypoglycemia refractory to 2-3 cycles of 15g sugar

Primary_Symptoms: High Blood Glucose (>250 mg/dL) with Ketosis and Metabolic Acidosis; Kussmaul deep rapid breathing; Fruity acetone breath odor
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain; Dehydration; Polyuria; Confusion; Lethargy; Coma; Tachycardia
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sugar >250 hai aur peshab me Ketone aaya hai?; 2. Saans me mitha/phala (fruity) jaisi badboo hai?; 3. Ulti, pet dard aur behoshi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Regular Insulin; IV Normal Saline 0.9%; Injection Potassium Chloride
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency IV fluids and IV Insulin protocol in ICU
Supportive_Medicines: ICU Admission; Aggressive IV Normal Saline hydration; Continuous IV Regular Insulin infusion (0.1 U/kg/h); Potassium replacement; Bicarbonate (if pH <6.9)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT attempt oral hydration or home insulin boluses if vomiting; Immediate ICU admission mandatory
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to tertiary hospital ICU; Keep patient lying on side if vomiting to prevent aspiration; Do NOT give oral food/drink
Lab_Investigations: Arterial Blood Gas (ABG - pH <7.3, HCO3 <18); Urine & Serum Ketones (Beta-hydroxybutyrate); Capillary Glucose; Serum Electrolytes (Potassium monitoring); RFT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; DKA diagnosis; Altered mental status/Coma; Anuria; Severe vomiting; Kussmaul breathing

Common_Names_Hindi: Sugar se naso me dard; Diabetic Neuropathy
Primary_Symptoms: Distal symmetrical 'glove-and-stocking' paresthesia: burning pain, tingling, numbness, shooting pains in feet/hands
Secondary_Symptoms: Loss of vibration/monofilament sensation; Dry cracked feet; Charcot joint; Allodynia (pain on light touch); Autonomic neuropathy
